cohort: 686,272 singleton live births in Austria between 2008 and 2016
finding: While not a direct causal factor, increased maternal age was associated with higher rates of cesarean sections, premature births, and other interventions during delivery, with parity playing a mediating role.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rates and surgically-assisted vaginal deliveries increased with advancing maternal age, while spontaneous delivery rates decreased.
